experienceIntro: A little about what I've been up to lately.

projects.title: EMIGRIA
description: EMIGRIA is an AI-powered platform designed to help prospective Indonesian migrant workers identify potential scams in overseas job vacancies. It analyzes job information, including salary offers, agency details, placement fees, and job requirements to identify potential warning signs.

The platform provides a fraud risk assessment to help users better understand whether a job opportunity is safe, suspicious, or potentially fraudulent, making overseas job verification more accessible and easier to understand.

projects.title: Lost n Found
projects.description: A modern campus lost-and-found platform powered by Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP), Gale-Shapley Stable Matching, and Groq Semantic AI, wrapped in a retro pixel-art pinboard interface.

experience.title: Data Science Cohort
experience.organization: DBS Foundation x Dicoding Coding Camp
experience.description: Contributed to the development of EMIGRIA, an end-to-end machine learning project focused on overseas job fraud detection. As part of the Data Science team, handled data collection, preprocessing, exploratory data analysis (EDA), feature engineering, model development, and evaluation. Also developed an interactive Streamlit dashboard to visualize analytical insights and present prediction results while collaborating with team members and mentors throughout the project.

about.heading: A little about me.
paragraphs: I'm an Informatics student at Gunadarma University with an interest in data, technology, and how things work behind the scenes.
I enjoy exploring data, experimenting with machine learning models, and building projects that turn ideas into something useful. I'm particularly interested in Data Science, Machine Learning, and AI.

Most of my experience comes from university projects, learning programs, and personal experiments. I'm always looking for opportunities to learn something new, try different approaches, and improve along the way.
